name: 2.6 Skewness and the Mean, Median, and Mode
_note: Complete on disk -- 10 questions. Seven were written 2026-08-09 and one more reused to finish the section. The whole section turns on one rule: skew is named for the TAIL, and the mean is dragged toward it. The drawn histogram makes the tail unmistakable rather than borderline, and the shape answer is computed from the same variable that sets the bar heights, so the picture and the key cannot disagree. The new ones cover the ordering of all three measures on a drawn shape, reading skew backwards out of a mean-median gap with no picture at all, naming skew from a box plot rather than a histogram, a two-peaked drawing, a computed demonstration that most of the data can fall below the mean, a diagnose-the-classmate question aimed straight at naming skew for the bulk instead of the tail, and a shape-center-spread capstone.

questions.title: Skewness and the Mean-Median Relationship - From a drawn histogram, identify skewed-left, skewed-right or symmetric, connect that shape to whether the mean is less than, greater than, or about equal to the median, and name a two-peaked distribution
Median Age Vs Life Expectancy - Explain why one town's lower median age reflects a younger population structure (birth rate), not a shorter lifespan, even under equal life expectancy
Skew Is Named for the Tail, Not the Bulk - Diagnose a classmate who named a skewed distribution backwards by looking at where the tall bars sit, and give the rule that fixes it
Order the Mean, Median and Mode on a Skewed Picture - From a drawn histogram, put the three measures of center in order along the axis and say which one the tail moves the most
Infer the Skew from the Mean and Median Alone - With no picture available, use the gap between the mean and the median to name the shape, then say which measure of center to report
Name the Skew from a Box Plot - Use the median's position in the box and the two whisker lengths to name the shape, then predict where the mean sits relative to the median
Identify a Bimodal Distribution - Spot two separate peaks in a drawn histogram, say why a single measure of center describes it badly, and name what usually causes two peaks

Why the Median Is the Honest Center for Skewed Data - Compute the mean and median of a right-skewed data set, count how many values actually fall below the mean, and decide which number a report should quote
Compare Two Distributions - Given summary statistics for two groups, identify which has the larger center and which the larger spread, and read the shape off the mean-median gap

Describe a Distribution - Shape, Center and Spread - Work through the three things a distribution is always described by, reading each one off the same drawn histogram, and choose the center that matches the shape you named
